entries.heading: About
entries.text: Gui is a fast, feature-rich terminal emulator for Windows: platform-native UI, GPU-accelerated rendering, with a parsing core from Ghostty. It is Ghostty on Windows, and then some. Why build Gui? As a project, we've decided to drop any roadmap for Windows support in the Ghostty GUI. Because the Ghostty team doesn't plan to do it. Spending my tokens means you don't have to spend yours. Judging by Ghostty's technical choices on the other two platforms, I think they would pick WinUI if they did it officially, so I picked WinUI.

entries.heading: 关于
entries.text: Gui 是一个快速、功能丰富的 Windows 终端模拟器：平台原生界面、GPU 加速渲染，解析内核来自 Ghostty。Windows 上的 Ghostty，又不止于此。 为什么做 Gui？ As a project, we've decided to drop any roadmap for Windows support in the Ghostty GUI. 因为 Ghostty 官方不打算做，所以我做。花我的 token，就不用花你们的 token。鉴于 Ghostty 官方在其他两个平台的技术选型，我觉得官方做的话会选择 WinUI，所以我选择 WinUI。

entries.heading: Option Reference
entries.text: This document is mostly based on Ghostty's Option Reference. This is a reference of all Gui configuration options. These options are ordered roughly by how common they are to be used and grouped with related options. I recommend utilizing your browser's search functionality to find the option you're looking for.

entries.heading: tab-position
entries.text: Where the tab rail sits — top, left or right.

entries.heading: compact
entries.text: true (default) runs panes edge to edge with 1 DIP dividers; false floats them as rounded cards.

entries.heading: sidebar-width-left
entries.text: The left tab rail's width in DIPs, written back by the app when you drag its edge.

entries.heading: sidebar-width-right
entries.text: The right tab rail's width in DIPs, written back by the app when you drag its edge.

entries.heading: debug-tap
entries.text: Record the raw VT byte stream in both directions as hex in the log.

entries.heading: crash-dumps
entries.text: Register with Windows Error Reporting for full dumps, left in %TEMP%\gui-dumps on a crash.

entries.heading: language
entries.text: Gui's graphical user interface language: en or zh-CN. For example: language = zh-CN An empty value (the default) follows the system language: a Simplified Chinese system gets the Chinese strings, any other language gets English. Unlike Ghostty, the value can be reloaded at runtime; no restart is needed. This only changes Gui's own interface text, not the language used by programs run _inside_ the terminal, which keep the system default.

entries.heading: font-family-bold-italic
entries.text: The font families to use. You can generate the list of valid values using the CLI: gui +list-fonts Inside Gui's own terminal the command opens a font browser: the installed families on the left, a preview drawn from the highlighted font's real outlines on the right, and Enter writes the chosen family into font-family in the config. When the output is redirected, or the command runs outside Gui, it prints one family per line with its styles instead. This configuration can be repeated multiple times to specify preferred fallback fonts when the requested codepoint is not available in the primary

entries.heading: font-style-bold-italic
entries.text: The named font style to use for each of the requested terminal font styles. This looks up the style based on the font style string advertised by the font itself. For example, "Iosevka Heavy" has a style of "Heavy". You can also use these fields to completely disable a font style. If you set the value of the configuration below to literal false then that font style will be disabled. If the running program in the terminal requests a disabled font style, the regular font style will be used instead. These are only valid if its corresponding font-family is also specified. If no font-family is speci

entries.heading: font-synthetic-style
entries.text: Control whether Gui should synthesize a style if the requested style is not available in the specified font-family. Gui can synthesize bold, italic, and bold italic styles if the font does not have a specific style. For bold, this is done by drawing an outline around the glyph of varying thickness. For italic, this is done by applying a slant to the glyph. For bold italic, both of these are applied. Synthetic styles are not perfect and will generally not look as good as a font that has the style natively. However, they are useful to provide styled text when the font does not have the style. Se

entries.heading: font-feature
entries.text: Apply a font feature. To enable multiple font features you can repeat this multiple times or use a comma-separated list of feature settings. The syntax for feature settings is as follows, where feat is a feature: Enable features with e.g. feat, +feat, feat on, feat=1. Disabled features with e.g. -feat, feat off, feat=0. Set a feature value with e.g. feat=2, feat = 3, feat 4. Feature names may be wrapped in quotes, meaning this config should be syntactically compatible with the font-feature-settings CSS property. The syntax is fairly loose, but invalid settings will be silently ignored. The fon

entries.heading: font-size
entries.text: Font size in points. This value can be a non-integer and the nearest integer pixel size will be selected. If you have a high dpi display where 1pt = 2px then you can get an odd numbered pixel size by specifying a half point. For example, 13.5pt @ 2px/pt = 27px Changing this configuration at runtime will only affect existing terminals that have NOT manually adjusted their font size in some way (e.g. increased or decreased the font size). Terminals that have manually adjusted their font size will retain their manually adjusted size. Otherwise, the font size of existing terminals will be updated

entries.heading: font-variation-bold-italic
entries.text: A repeatable configuration to set one or more font variations values for a variable font. A variable font is a single font, usually with a filename ending in -VF.ttf or -VF.otf that contains one or more configurable axes for things such as weight, slant, etc. Not all fonts support variations; only fonts that explicitly state they are variable fonts will work. The format of this is id=value where id is the axis identifier. An axis identifier is always a 4 character string, such as wght. To get the list of supported axes, look at your font documentation or use a font inspection tool. Invalid ids

entries.heading: font-codepoint-map
entries.text: Force one or a range of Unicode codepoints to map to a specific named font. This is useful if you want to support special symbols or if you want to use specific glyphs that render better for your specific font. The syntax is codepoint=fontname where codepoint is either a single codepoint or a range. Codepoints must be specified as full Unicode hex values, such as U+ABCD. Codepoints ranges are specified as U+ABCD-U+DEFG. You can specify multiple ranges for the same font separated by commas, such as U+ABCD-U+DEFG,U+1234-U+5678=fontname. The font name is the same value as you would use for font-f

entries.heading: clipboard-codepoint-map
entries.text: Map specific Unicode codepoints to replacement values when copying text to clipboard. This configuration allows you to replace specific Unicode characters with other characters or strings when copying terminal content to the clipboard. This is useful for converting special terminal symbols to more compatible characters for pasting into other applications. The syntax is similar to font-codepoint-map: Single codepoint: U+1234=U+ABCD or U+1234=replacement_text Codepoint range: U+1234-U+5678=U+ABCD Examples: clipboard-codepoint-map = U+2500=U+002D (box drawing horizontal → hyphen) clipboard-codepo

entries.heading: font-shaping-break
entries.text: Locations to break font shaping into multiple runs. A "run" is a contiguous segment of text that is shaped together. "Shaping" is the process of converting text (codepoints) into glyphs (renderable characters). This is how ligatures are formed, among other things. For example, if a coding font turns "!=" into a single glyph, then it must see "!" and "=" next to each other in a single run. When a run is broken, the text is shaped separately. To continue our example, if "!" is at the end of one run and "=" is at the start of the next run, then the ligature will not be formed. Gui breaks runs at

entries.heading: adjust-cell-height
entries.text: All of the configurations behavior adjust various metrics determined by the font. The values can be integers (1, -1, etc.) or a percentage (20%, -15%, etc.). In each case, the values represent the amount to change the original value. For example, a value of 1 increases the value by 1; it does not set it to literally 1. A value of 20% increases the value by 20%. And so on. There is little to no validation on these values so the wrong values (e.g. -100%) can cause the terminal to be unusable. Use with caution and reason. Some values are clamped to minimum or maximum values. This can make it appe

entries.heading: adjust-font-baseline
entries.text: Distance in pixels or percentage adjustment from the bottom of the cell to the text baseline. Increase to move baseline UP, decrease to move baseline DOWN. See the notes about adjustments in adjust-cell-width.

entries.heading: adjust-underline-position
entries.text: Distance in pixels or percentage adjustment from the top of the cell to the top of the underline. Increase to move underline DOWN, decrease to move underline UP. See the notes about adjustments in adjust-cell-width.

entries.heading: adjust-underline-thickness
entries.text: Thickness in pixels of the underline. See the notes about adjustments in adjust-cell-width.

entries.heading: adjust-strikethrough-position
entries.text: Distance in pixels or percentage adjustment from the top of the cell to the top of the strikethrough. Increase to move strikethrough DOWN, decrease to move strikethrough UP. See the notes about adjustments in adjust-cell-width.

entries.heading: adjust-strikethrough-thickness
entries.text: Thickness in pixels or percentage adjustment of the strikethrough. See the notes about adjustments in adjust-cell-width.

entries.heading: adjust-overline-position
entries.text: Distance in pixels or percentage adjustment from the top of the cell to the top of the overline. Increase to move overline DOWN, decrease to move overline UP. See the notes about adjustments in adjust-cell-width.

entries.heading: adjust-overline-thickness
entries.text: Thickness in pixels or percentage adjustment of the overline. See the notes about adjustments in adjust-cell-width.

entries.heading: adjust-cursor-thickness
entries.text: Thickness in pixels or percentage adjustment of the bar cursor and outlined rect cursor. See the notes about adjustments in adjust-cell-width.

entries.heading: adjust-cursor-height
entries.text: Height in pixels or percentage adjustment of the cursor. Currently applies to all cursor types: bar, rect, and outlined rect. See the notes about adjustments in adjust-cell-width.

entries.heading: adjust-box-thickness
entries.text: Thickness in pixels or percentage adjustment of box drawing characters. See the notes about adjustments in adjust-cell-width.

entries.heading: adjust-icon-height
entries.text: Height in pixels or percentage adjustment of maximum height for nerd font icons. A positive (negative) value will increase (decrease) the maximum icon height. This may not affect all icons equally: the effect depends on whether the default size of the icon is height-constrained, which in turn depends on the aspect ratio of both the icon and your primary font. Certain icons designed for box drawing and terminal graphics, such as Powerline symbols, are not affected by this option. See the notes about adjustments in adjust-cell-width.

entries.heading: theme
entries.text: The theme to use: a built-in theme name, or the name of a file in your themes folder. Gui also supports specifying a different theme for light and dark mode. A theme name is resolved by file name: first in the themes folder beside the config file (%APPDATA%\gui\themes), then in the bundled Assets\Themes\light and Assets\Themes\dark folders next to the executable. A theme in your own folder replaces a bundled theme of the same name. Names may not contain path separators, and theme takes a name rather than a path. To see a list of available themes, run gui +list-themes. A theme file sets colours

entries.heading: background
entries.text: Background color for the window. Specified as either hex (#RRGGBB or RRGGBB) or a named X11 color.

entries.heading: foreground
entries.text: Foreground color for the window. Specified as either hex (#RRGGBB or RRGGBB) or a named X11 color.

entries.heading: background-image
entries.text: Background image for the terminal. This should be a path to a PNG or JPEG file, other image formats are not yet supported. The background image is currently per-terminal, not per-window. The decoded image is shared by every pane in the process, so splits draw the same bitmap instead of duplicating it in VRAM.

entries.heading: background-image-opacity
entries.text: Background image opacity. This is relative to the value of background-opacity. Gui handles this differently from Ghostty. The value accepts 0.0 to 1.0; anything above 1.0 is treated as 1.0. The image is drawn at this opacity multiplied by background-opacity, layered on top of the pane surface. With the default background-opacity = 1.0 the image is simply placed on top of the background color. At lower background opacities the image is layered over the already translucent pane, so it ends up noticeably more opaque than the pane background itself. Ghostty instead composites the image with the ba

entries.heading: background-image-position
entries.text: Background image position. Valid values are: top-left top-center top-right center-left center center-right bottom-left bottom-center bottom-right The default value is center.

entries.heading: background-image-fit
entries.text: Background image fit. Valid values are: contain Preserving the aspect ratio, scale the background image to the largest size that can still be contained within the terminal, so that the whole image is visible. cover Preserving the aspect ratio, scale the background image to the smallest size that can completely cover the terminal. This may result in one or more edges of the image being clipped by the edge of the terminal. stretch Stretch the background image to the full size of the terminal, without preserving the aspect ratio. none Don't scale the background image. The default value is contain

entries.heading: background-image-repeat
entries.text: Whether to repeat the background image or not. If this is set to true, the background image will be repeated if there would otherwise be blank space around it because it doesn't completely fill the terminal area. The default value is false.

entries.heading: selection-background
entries.text: The foreground and background color for selection. If this is not set, then the selection color is just the inverted window background and foreground (note: not to be confused with the cell bg/fg). Specified as either hex (#RRGGBB or RRGGBB) or a named X11 color.

entries.heading: selection-clear-on-typing
entries.text: Whether to clear selected text when typing. This defaults to true. This is typical behavior for most terminal emulators as well as text input fields. If you set this to false, then the selected text will not be cleared when typing. "Typing" is specifically defined as any non-modifier (shift, control, alt, etc.) keypress that produces data to be sent to the application running within the terminal (e.g. the shell). Additionally, selection is cleared when any preedit or composition state is started (e.g. when typing languages such as Japanese). If this is false, then the selection can still be ma

entries.heading: selection-clear-on-copy
entries.text: Whether to clear selected text after copying. This defaults to false. When set to true, the selection will be automatically cleared after any copy operation that invokes the copy_to_clipboard keyboard binding. Importantly, this will not clear the selection if the copy operation was invoked via copy-on-select. When set to false, the selection remains visible after copying, allowing to see what was copied and potentially perform additional operations on the same selection.

entries.heading: selection-word-chars
entries.text: Characters that mark word boundaries during text selection operations such as double-clicking. When selecting a word, the selection will stop at any of these characters. This is similar to the WORDCHARS environment variable in zsh, except this specifies the boundary characters rather than the word characters. The default includes common delimiters and punctuation that typically separate words in code and prose. Each character in this string becomes a word boundary. Multi-byte UTF-8 characters are supported, but only single codepoints can be specified. Multi-codepoint sequences (e.g. emoji) are

entries.heading: minimum-contrast
entries.text: The minimum contrast ratio between the foreground and background colors. The contrast ratio is a value between 1 and 21. A value of 1 allows for no contrast (e.g. black on black). This value is the contrast ratio as defined by the WCAG 2.0 specification. If you want to avoid invisible text (same color as background), a value of 1.1 is a good value. If you want to avoid text that is difficult to read, a value of 3 or higher is a good value. The higher the value, the more likely that text will become black or white. This value does not apply to Emoji or images.

entries.heading: palette
entries.text: Color palette for the 256 color form that many terminal applications use. The syntax of this configuration is N=COLOR where N is 0 to 255 (for the 256 colors in the terminal color table) and COLOR is a typical RGB color code such as #AABBCC or AABBCC, or a named X11 color. For example, palette = 5=#BB78D9 will set the 'purple' color. The palette index can be in decimal, binary, octal, or hexadecimal. Decimal is assumed unless a prefix is used: 0b for binary, 0o for octal, and 0x for hexadecimal. For definitions on the color indices and what they canonically map to, see this cheat sheet. For mo

entries.heading: palette-generate
entries.text: Whether to automatically generate the extended 256 color palette (indices 16–255) from the base 16 ANSI colors. This lets theme authors specify only the base 16 colors and have the rest of the palette be automatically generated in a consistent and aesthetic way. When enabled, the 6×6×6 color cube and 24-step grayscale ramp are derived from interpolations of the base palette, giving a more cohesive look. Colors that have been explicitly set via palette are never overwritten. The default value is false (disabled), because many legacy programs using the 256-color palette hardcode assumptions abou

entries.heading: palette-harmonious
entries.text: Invert the palette colors generated when palette-generate is enabled, so that the colors go in reverse order. This allows palette-based applications to work well in both light and dark mode since the palettes are always relatively good colors. This defaults to off because some legacy terminal applications hardcode the assumption that palette indices 16–231 are ordered from darkest to lightest, so enabling this would make them unreadable. This is not a generally good assumption and we encourage modern terminal applications to use the indices in a more semantic way. This has no effect if palette

entries.heading: cursor-color
entries.text: The color of the cursor. If this is not set, a default will be chosen. Direct colors can be specified as either hex (#RRGGBB or RRGGBB) or a named X11 color. Additionally, special values can be used to set the color to match other colors at runtime: cell-foreground - Match the cell foreground color. cell-background - Match the cell background color.

entries.heading: cursor-opacity
entries.text: The opacity level (opposite of transparency) of the cursor. A value of 1 is fully opaque and a value of 0 is fully transparent. A value less than 0 or greater than 1 will be clamped to the nearest valid value. Note that a sufficiently small value such as 0.3 may be effectively invisible and may make it difficult to find the cursor.

entries.heading: cursor-style
entries.text: The style of the cursor. This sets the default style. A running program can still request an explicit cursor style using escape sequences (such as CSI q). Shell configurations will often request specific cursor styles. Note that shell integration will automatically set the cursor to a bar at a prompt, regardless of this configuration. You can disable that behavior by specifying shell-integration-features = no-cursor or disabling shell integration entirely. Valid values are: block bar underline block_hollow

entries.heading: cursor-style-blink
entries.text: Sets the default blinking state of the cursor. This is just the default state; running programs may override the cursor style using DECSCUSR (CSI q). If this is not set, the cursor does not blink by default. Set it to true to make it blink. Valid values are: (blank) true false

entries.heading: cursor-text
entries.text: The color of the text under the cursor. If this is not set, a default will be chosen. Specified as either hex (#RRGGBB or RRGGBB) or a named X11 color. This can also be set to cell-foreground to match the cell foreground color, or cell-background to match the cell background color.

entries.heading: mouse-hide-while-typing
entries.text: Hide the mouse immediately when typing. The mouse becomes visible again when the mouse is used (button, movement, etc.).

entries.heading: scroll-to-bottom
entries.text: When to scroll the surface to the bottom. The format of this is a list of options to enable separated by commas. If you prefix an option with no- then it is disabled. If you omit an option, its default value is used. Available options: keystroke If set, scroll the surface to the bottom when the user presses a key that results in data being sent to the PTY (basically anything but modifiers or keybinds that are processed by Gui). output If set, scroll the surface to the bottom if there is new data to display (e.g., when new lines are printed to the terminal). The default is keystroke, no-output.

entries.heading: mouse-shift-capture
entries.text: Determines whether running programs can detect the shift key pressed with a mouse click. Typically, the shift key is used to extend mouse selection. The default value of false means that the shift key is not sent with the mouse protocol and will extend the selection. This value can be conditionally overridden by the running program with the XTSHIFTESCAPE sequence. The value true means that the shift key is sent with the mouse protocol but the running program can override this behavior with XTSHIFTESCAPE. The value never is the same as false but the running program cannot override this behavior

entries.heading: mouse-reporting
entries.text: Enable or disable mouse reporting. When set to false, mouse events will not be reported to terminal applications even if they request it. This allows you to always use the mouse for selection and other terminal UI interactions without applications capturing mouse input. When set to true (the default), terminal applications can request mouse reporting and will receive mouse events according to their requested mode. This can be toggled at runtime using the toggle_mouse_reporting keybind action.

entries.heading: mouse-scroll-multiplier
entries.text: Multiplier for scrolling distance with the mouse wheel. A prefix of precision: or discrete: can be used to set the multiplier only for scrolling with the specific type of devices. These can be comma-separated to set both types of multipliers at the same time, e.g. precision:0.1,discrete:3. If no prefix is used, the multiplier applies to all scrolling devices. Specifying a prefix was introduced in Gui 1.2.1. The value will be clamped to [0.01, 10,000]. Both of these are extreme and you're likely to have a bad experience if you set either extreme. The default value is "3" for discrete devices an

entries.heading: background-opacity
entries.text: The opacity level (opposite of transparency) of the background. A value of 1 is fully opaque and a value of 0 is fully transparent. A value less than 0 or greater than 1 will be clamped to the nearest valid value. Gui Below 1 the whole window, chrome included, is tinted once instead of stacking on the system acrylic; background-blur picks acrylic or a plain tint.

entries.heading: background-opacity-cells
entries.text: Applies background opacity to cells with an explicit background color set. Normally, background-opacity is only applied to the window background. If a cell has an explicit background color set, such as red, then that background color will be fully opaque. An effect of this is that some terminal applications that repaint the background color of the terminal such as a Neovim and Tmux may not respect the background-opacity (by design). Setting this to true will apply the background-opacity to all cells regardless of whether they have an explicit background color set or not.

entries.heading: background-blur
entries.text: Whether to blur the background when background-opacity is less than 1. Valid values are: a nonnegative integer specifying the blur intensity false, equivalent to a blur intensity of 0 true, equivalent to the default blur intensity of 20, which is reasonable for a good looking blur. Higher blur intensities may cause strange rendering and performance issues. Gui true uses acrylic; false paints an unblurred tint on Windows 11 (Windows 10 keeps acrylic, as Windows Terminal does).

entries.heading: unfocused-split-opacity
entries.text: The opacity level (opposite of transparency) of an unfocused split. Unfocused splits by default are slightly faded out to make it easier to see which split is focused. To disable this feature, set this value to 1. A value of 1 is fully opaque and a value of 0 is fully transparent. Because "0" is not useful (it makes the window look very weird), the minimum value is 0.15. This value still looks weird but you can at least see what's going on. A value outside of the range 0.15 to 1 will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

entries.heading: unfocused-split-fill
entries.text: The color to dim the unfocused split. Unfocused splits are dimmed by rendering a semi-transparent rectangle over the split. This sets the color of that rectangle and can be used to carefully control the dimming effect. This will default to the background color. Specified as either hex (#RRGGBB or RRGGBB) or a named X11 color.

entries.heading: split-divider-color
entries.text: The color of the split divider. If this is not set, a default will be chosen. Specified as either hex (#RRGGBB or RRGGBB) or a named X11 color.

entries.heading: search-background
entries.text: The foreground and background color for search matches. This only applies to non-focused search matches, also known as candidate matches. Valid values: Hex (#RRGGBB or RRGGBB) Named X11 color "cell-foreground" to match the cell foreground color "cell-background" to match the cell background color The default value is black text on a golden yellow background.

entries.heading: search-selected-background
entries.text: The foreground and background color for the currently selected search match. This is the focused match that will be jumped to when using next/previous search navigation. Valid values: Hex (#RRGGBB or RRGGBB) Named X11 color "cell-foreground" to match the cell foreground color "cell-background" to match the cell background color The default value is black text on a soft peach background.

entries.heading: command
entries.text: The command to run, usually a shell. If this is not an absolute path, it'll be looked up in the PATH. If this is not set, a default will be looked up from your system. The rules for the default lookup are: SHELL environment variable passwd entry (user information) This can contain additional arguments to run the command with. If additional arguments are provided, the command will be executed using /bin/sh -c to offload shell argument expansion. To avoid shell expansion altogether, prefix the command with direct:, e.g. direct:nvim foo. This will avoid the roundtrip to /bin/sh but will also not

entries.heading: initial-command
entries.text: This is the same as "command", but only applies to the first terminal surface created when Gui starts. Subsequent terminal surfaces will use the command configuration. After the first terminal surface is created (or closed), there is no way to run this initial command again automatically. As such, setting this at runtime works but will only affect the next terminal surface if it is the first one ever created. If you start Gui from the command line, -e is a shortcut for this configuration: every argument after it becomes the command. For example: gui -e fish --with --custom --args.

entries.heading: notify-on-command-finish
entries.text: Controls when command finished notifications are sent. There are three options: never - Never send notifications. unfocused - Only send notifications if the surface that the command is running in is not focused (the default). always - Always send notifications. Command finished notifications requires that either shell integration is enabled, or that your shell sends OSC 133 escape sequences to mark the start and end of commands.

entries.heading: notify-on-command-finish-action
entries.text: If command finished notifications are enabled, this controls how the user is notified. Available options: bell - enabled by default notify - enabled by default Options can be combined by listing them as a comma separated list. Options can be negated by prefixing them with no-. For example no-bell,notify.

entries.heading: notify-on-command-finish-after
entries.text: If command finished notifications are enabled, this controls how long a command must have been running before a notification will be sent. The default is five seconds. The duration is specified as a series of numbers followed by time units. Whitespace is allowed between numbers and units. Each number and unit will be added together to form the total duration. The allowed time units are as follows: y - 365 SI days, or 8760 hours, or 31536000 seconds. No adjustments are made for leap years or leap seconds. d - one SI day, or 86400 seconds. h - one hour, or 3600 seconds. m - one minute, or 60 sec

entries.heading: env
entries.text: Extra environment variables to pass to commands launched in a terminal surface. The format is env=KEY=VALUE. env = foo=bar env = bar=baz Setting env to an empty string will reset the entire map to default (empty). env = Setting a key to an empty string will remove that particular key and corresponding value from the map. env = foo=bar env = foo= will result in foo not being passed to the launched commands. Setting a key multiple times will overwrite previous entries. env = foo=bar env = foo=baz will result in foo=baz being passed to the launched commands. These environment variables will overr

entries.heading: input
entries.text: Data to send as input to the command on startup. The configured command will be launched using the typical rules, then the data specified as this input will be written to the pty before any other input can be provided. The bytes are sent as-is with no additional encoding. Therefore, be cautious about input that can contain control characters, because this can be used to execute programs in a shell. The format of this value is: raw: - Send raw text as-is. This uses Zig string literal syntax so you can specify control characters and other standard escapes. path: - Read a filepath and send the co

entries.heading: wait-after-command
entries.text: If true, keep the terminal open after the command exits. Normally, the terminal window closes when the running command (such as a shell) exits. With this true, the terminal window will stay open until any keypress is received. This is primarily useful for scripts or debugging.

entries.heading: abnormal-command-exit-runtime
entries.text: The number of milliseconds of runtime below which we consider a process exit to be abnormal. This is used to show an error message when the process exits too quickly.

entries.heading: scrollbar
entries.text: Control when the scrollbar is shown to scroll the scrollback buffer. The default value is system. Valid values: system - Respect the system settings for when to show scrollbars. never - Never show a scrollbar. You can still scroll using the mouse, keybind actions, etc. but you will not have a visual UI widget showing a scrollbar.

entries.heading: link-url
entries.text: Enable URL matching. URLs are matched on hover with Ctrl pressed and open using the default system application for the linked URL. Gui matches URLs only; there are no custom link rules.

entries.heading: link-previews
entries.text: Show link previews for a matched URL. When true, link previews are shown for all matched URLs. When false, link previews are never shown. When set to "osc8", link previews are only shown for hyperlinks created with the OSC 8 sequence (in this case, the link text can differ from the link destination).

entries.heading: maximize
entries.text: Whether to start the window in a maximized state. This setting applies to new windows and does not apply to tabs, splits, etc. However, this setting will apply to all new windows, not just the first one.

entries.heading: fullscreen
entries.text: Start new windows in fullscreen. This setting applies to new windows and does not apply to tabs, splits, etc. However, this setting will apply to all new windows, not just the first one. Allowable values are: false - Don't start in fullscreen (default) true - Start in native fullscreen

entries.heading: title
entries.text: The title Gui will use for the window. This will force the title of the window to be this title at all times and Gui will ignore any set title escape sequences programs (such as Neovim) may send. If you want a blank title, set this to one or more spaces by quoting the value. For example, title = " ". This effectively hides the title. This is necessary because setting a blank value resets the title to the default value of the running program. This configuration can be reloaded at runtime. If it is set, the title will update for all windows. If it is unset, the next title change escape sequence

entries.heading: working-directory
entries.text: The directory to change to after starting the command. This setting is secondary to the window-inherit-working-directory setting. If a previous Gui terminal exists in the same process, window-inherit-working-directory will take precedence. Otherwise, this setting will be used. Typically, this setting is used only for the first window. The default is inherit. The value of this must be an absolute path, a path prefixed with ~/ (the tilde will be expanded to the user's home directory), or one of the special values below: home - The home directory of the executing user. inherit - The working direc

entries.heading: keybind
entries.text: Key bindings. The format is trigger=action. Duplicate triggers will overwrite previously set values. The list of actions is available in the action reference. Trigger: +-separated list of keys and modifiers. Example: ctrl+a, ctrl+shift+b, up. If the key is a single Unicode codepoint, the trigger will match any presses that produce that codepoint. These are impacted by keyboard layouts. For example, a will match the a key on a QWERTY keyboard, but will match the q key on a AZERTY keyboard (assuming US physical layout). For Unicode codepoints, matching is done by comparing the set of modifiers w

entries.heading: key-remap
entries.text: Remap modifier keys within Gui. This allows you to swap or reassign modifier keys at the application level without affecting system-wide settings. The format is from=to where both from and to are modifier key names. You can use generic names like ctrl, alt, shift, super or sided names like left_ctrl, right_alt, etc. This will NOT change keyboard layout or key encodings outside of Gui. Example: key-remap = ctrl=super key-remap = left_control=right_alt Important notes: This is a one-way remap. If you remap ctrl=super, then the physical Ctrl key acts as Super, but the Super key remains Super. Rem

entries.heading: window-padding-x
entries.text: Horizontal window padding. This applies padding between the terminal cells and the left and right window borders. The value is in points, meaning that it will be scaled appropriately for screen DPI. If this value is set too large, the screen will render nothing, because the grid will be completely squished by the padding. It is up to you as the user to pick a reasonable value. If you pick an unreasonable value, a warning will appear in the logs. Changing this configuration at runtime will only affect new terminals, i.e. new windows, tabs, etc. To set a different left and right padding, specify

entries.heading: window-padding-y
entries.text: Vertical window padding. This applies padding between the terminal cells and the top and bottom window borders. The value is in points, meaning that it will be scaled appropriately for screen DPI. If this value is set too large, the screen will render nothing, because the grid will be completely squished by the padding. It is up to you as the user to pick a reasonable value. If you pick an unreasonable value, a warning will appear in the logs. Changing this configuration at runtime will only affect new terminals, i.e. new windows, tabs, etc. To set a different top and bottom padding, specify t

entries.heading: window-padding-balance
entries.text: The viewport dimensions are usually not perfectly divisible by the cell size. In this case, some extra padding on the end of a column and the bottom of the final row may exist. If this is true, then this extra padding is automatically balanced between all four edges to minimize imbalance on one side. If this is false, the top left grid cell will always hug the edge with zero padding other than what may be specified with the other window-padding options. If other window-padding fields are set and this is true, this will still apply. The other padding is applied first and may affect how many gri

entries.heading: window-inherit-working-directory
entries.text: If true, new windows will inherit the working directory of the previously focused window. If no window was previously focused, the default working directory will be used (the working-directory option).

entries.heading: tab-inherit-working-directory
entries.text: If true, new tabs will inherit the working directory of the previously focused tab. If no tab was previously focused, the default working directory will be used (the working-directory option).

entries.heading: split-inherit-working-directory
entries.text: If true, new split panes will inherit the working directory of the previously focused split. If no split was previously focused, the default working directory will be used (the working-directory option).

entries.heading: window-inherit-font-size
entries.text: If true, new windows and tabs will inherit the font size of the previously focused window. If no window was previously focused, the default font size will be used. If this is false, the default font size specified in the configuration font-size will be used.

entries.heading: window-title-font-family
entries.text: The font that will be used for the application's window and tab titles. If this setting is left unset, the system default font will be used. any font available on the system may be used, this font is not required to be a fixed-width font.

entries.heading: window-theme
entries.text: The theme to use for the windows. Valid values: system - Use the system theme. light - Use the light theme regardless of system theme. dark - Use the dark theme regardless of system theme. Gui Gui accepts system (default), light or dark only. The window chrome is a neutral surface: it never takes the terminal's background, and the terminal theme never repaints it.

entries.heading: window-width
entries.text: The initial window size. This size is in terminal grid cells by default. Both values must be set to take effect. If only one value is set, it is ignored. We don't currently support specifying a size in pixels but a future change can enable that. If this isn't specified, the app runtime will determine some default size. Note that the window manager may put limits on the size or override the size. For example, a tiling window manager may force the window to be a certain size to fit within the grid. There is nothing Gui will do about this, but it will make an effort. Sizes larger than the screen

entries.heading: window-position-y
entries.text: The starting window position. This position is in pixels and is relative to the top-left corner of the primary monitor. Both values must be set to take effect. If only one value is set, it is ignored. Note that the window manager may put limits on the position or override the position. For example, a tiling window manager may force the window to be a certain position to fit within the grid. There is nothing Gui will do about this, but it will make an effort. Also note that negative values are also up to the operating system and window manager. Some window managers may not allow windows to be p

entries.heading: window-save-state
entries.text: Whether to enable saving and restoring window state. Window state includes their position, size, tabs, splits, etc. Some window state requires shell integration, such as preserving working directories. See shell-integration for more information. There are two valid values for this configuration: never will never save window state. always will always save window state whenever Gui is exited. If you change this value to never while Gui is not running, the next Gui launch will NOT restore the window state. If you change this value so that window state is saved while Gui is not running, the previo

entries.heading: window-new-tab-position
entries.text: The position where new tabs are created. Valid values: current - Insert the new tab after the currently focused tab, or at the end if there are no focused tabs. end - Insert the new tab at the end of the tab list.

entries.heading: window-show-tab-bar
entries.text: Whether to show the tab bar. Valid values: always (default) Always display the tab bar, even when there's only one tab. auto Automatically show and hide the tab bar. The tab bar is only shown when there are two or more tabs present. never Never show the tab bar. Tabs are only accessible via the tab overview or by keybind actions. Gui Gui only distinguishes never from the other values: auto behaves like always.

entries.heading: focus-follows-mouse
entries.text: If true, when there are multiple split panes, the mouse selects the pane that is focused. This only applies to the currently focused window; e.g. mousing over a split in an unfocused window will not focus that split and bring the window to front. Default is false.

entries.heading: clipboard-read
entries.text: Gui allow or deny. ask has no blocking prompt in this build, so it behaves like deny.

entries.heading: clipboard-write
entries.text: Whether to allow programs running in the terminal to read/write to the system clipboard (OSC 52, for googling). Reading defaults to ask and writing defaults to allow; in this build ask has no blocking prompt, so reading behaves like deny. Valid values are: ask allow deny

entries.heading: clipboard-trim-trailing-spaces
entries.text: Trims trailing whitespace on data that is copied to the clipboard. This does not affect data sent to the clipboard via clipboard-write. This only applies to trailing whitespace on lines that have other characters. Completely blank lines always have their whitespace trimmed.

entries.heading: clipboard-paste-protection
entries.text: Require confirmation before pasting text that appears unsafe. This helps prevent a "copy/paste attack" where a user may accidentally execute unsafe commands by pasting text with newlines.

entries.heading: clipboard-paste-bracketed-safe
entries.text: If true, bracketed pastes will be considered safe. By default, bracketed pastes are considered safe. "Bracketed" pastes are pastes while the running program has bracketed paste mode enabled (a setting set by the running program, not the terminal emulator).

entries.heading: title-report
entries.text: Enables or disabled title reporting (CSI 21 t). This escape sequence allows the running program to query the terminal title. This is a common security issue and is disabled by default. This can expose sensitive information at best and enable arbitrary code execution at worst (with a maliciously crafted title and a minor amount of user interaction).

entries.heading: image-storage-limit
entries.text: The total amount of bytes that can be used for image data (e.g. the Kitty image protocol) per terminal screen. The maximum value is 4,294,967,295 (4GiB). The default is 320MB. If this is set to zero, then all image protocols will be disabled. This value is separate for primary and alternate screens so the effective limit per surface is double.

entries.heading: copy-on-select
entries.text: Whether to automatically copy selected text to the clipboard. true will prefer to copy to the selection clipboard, otherwise it will copy to the system clipboard. The value clipboard will always copy text to the selection clipboard as well as the system clipboard. Middle-click paste will always use the selection clipboard. Middle-click paste is always enabled even if this is false. The default value is false. Gui none, primary, clipboard or both. Windows has no selection clipboard, so primary does nothing and both copies to the system clipboard.

entries.heading: right-click-action
entries.text: The action to take when the user right-clicks on the terminal surface. Valid values: context-menu - Show the context menu. paste - Paste the contents of the clipboard. copy - Copy the selected text to the clipboard. copy-or-paste - If there is a selection, copy the selected text to the clipboard; otherwise, paste the contents of the clipboard. ignore - Do nothing, ignore the right-click. The default value is context-menu.

entries.heading: click-repeat-interval
entries.text: The time in milliseconds between clicks to consider a click a repeat (double, triple, etc.) or an entirely new single click. A value of zero will use a platform-specific default; 500ms on Windows.

entries.heading: config-file
entries.text: Additional configuration files to read. This configuration can be repeated to read multiple configuration files. Configuration files themselves can load more configuration files. Paths are relative to the file containing the config-file directive. For command-line arguments, paths are relative to the current working directory. Prepend a ? character to the file path to suppress errors if the file does not exist. If you want to include a file that begins with a literal ? character, surround the file path in double quotes ("). Cycles are not allowed. If a cycle is detected, an error will be logge

entries.heading: config-default-files
entries.text: When this is true, the default configuration file is loaded. That file is %APPDATA%\gui\config (C:\Users\ \AppData\Roaming\gui\config). If this is false, the default configuration file is not loaded; only the files given with --config-file are read. This is a CLI-only configuration. Setting it in a configuration file has no effect: Gui reports it as an unknown option and ignores it. It can only be set via command-line arguments.

entries.heading: confirm-close-surface
entries.text: Confirms that a surface should be closed before closing it. This defaults to true. If set to false, surfaces will close without any confirmation. This can also be set to always, which will always confirm closing a surface, even if shell integration says a process isn't running.

entries.heading: quick-terminal-position
entries.text: The position of the "quick" terminal window. To learn more about the quick terminal, see the documentation for the toggle_quick_terminal binding action. Valid values are: top - Terminal appears at the top of the screen. bottom - Terminal appears at the bottom of the screen. left - Terminal appears at the left of the screen. right - Terminal appears at the right of the screen. center - Terminal appears at the center of the screen. Each time the quick terminal is shown it re-reads the config, so a new position takes effect on the next reveal without a restart. There is no default keybind for tog

entries.heading: quick-terminal-size
entries.text: The size of the quick terminal. The size can be specified either as a percentage of the screen dimensions (height/width), or as an absolute size in pixels. Percentage values are suffixed with % (e.g. 20%) while pixel values are suffixed with px (e.g. 300px). A bare value without a suffix is ignored and the default size is used. When only one size is specified, the size parameter affects the size of the quick terminal on its primary axis, which depends on its position: height for quick terminals placed on the top or bottom, and width for left or right. The primary axis of a centered quick termi

entries.heading: quick-terminal-screen
entries.text: The screen where the quick terminal should show up. Valid values are: main - The screen that the operating system recommends as the main screen (DisplayArea.Primary). This screen is defined by the operating system and not chosen by Gui. mouse - The screen that the mouse is currently hovered over. The default value is mouse. Any other value, including Ghostty's macos-menu-bar, is treated as mouse.

entries.heading: quick-terminal-animation-duration
entries.text: Duration (in seconds) of the quick terminal enter and exit animation. The default is 0.2. Set it to 0 to disable animation completely. The config is re-read each time the terminal is shown, so it can be changed at runtime.

entries.heading: quick-terminal-autohide
entries.text: Automatically hide the quick terminal when focus shifts to another window. The default is true. Set it to false for the quick terminal to remain open even when it loses focus.

entries.heading: shell-integration
entries.text: Whether to enable shell integration auto-injection or not. Shell integration greatly enhances the terminal experience by enabling a number of features: Working directory reporting so new tabs, splits inherit the previous terminal's working directory. Prompt marking that enables the "jump_to_prompt" keybinding. If you're sitting at a prompt, closing a terminal will not ask for confirmation. Resizing the window with a complex prompt usually paints much better. Allowable values are: none - Do not do any automatic injection. You can still manually configure your shell to enable the integration. de

entries.heading: shell-integration-features
entries.text: Shell integration features to enable. These require our shell integration to be loaded, either automatically via shell-integration or manually. The format of this is a list of features to enable separated by commas. If you prefix a feature with no- then it is disabled. If you omit a feature, its default value is used. You can also use true or false to turn all features on or off. Example: cursor, no-cursor, title, no-title Available features: cursor - Set the cursor to a bar at the prompt (enabled by default). Add :steady to ask for a steady bar that does not blink, e.g. cursor:steady. title -

entries.heading: osc-color-report-format
entries.text: Sets the reporting format for OSC sequences that request color information. Gui currently supports OSC 10 (foreground), OSC 11 (background), and OSC 4 (256 color palette) queries, and by default the reported values are scaled-up RGB values, where each component are 16 bits. This is how most terminals report these values. However, some legacy applications may require 8-bit, unscaled, components. We also support turning off reporting altogether. The components are lowercase hex values. Allowable values are: none - OSC 4/10/11 queries receive no reply 8-bit - Color components are return unscaled,

entries.heading: vt-kam-allowed
entries.text: If true, allows the "KAM" mode (ANSI mode 2) to be used within the terminal. KAM disables keyboard input at the request of the application. This is not a common feature and is not recommended to be enabled. This will not be documented further because if you know you need KAM, you know. If you don't know if you need KAM, you don't need it.

entries.heading: custom-shader
entries.text: Custom shaders to run after the default shaders. This is a file path to a GLSL-syntax shader for all platforms. Invalid shaders can cause Gui to become unusable such as by causing the window to be completely black. If this happens, you can unset this configuration to disable the shader. Custom shader support is based on and compatible with the Shadertoy shaders. Shaders should specify a mainImage function and the available uniforms largely match Shadertoy, with some caveats and Gui-specific extensions. The uniform values available to shaders are as follows: sampler2D iChannel0 - Input texture.

entries.heading: custom-shader-animation
entries.text: If true (default), the focused terminal surface will run an animation loop when custom shaders are used. This uses slightly more CPU (generally less than 10%) but allows the shader to animate. This only runs if there are custom shaders and the terminal is focused. If this is set to false, the terminal and custom shader will only render when the terminal is updated. This is more efficient but the shader will not animate. This can also be set to always, which will always run the animation loop regardless of whether the terminal is focused or not. The animation loop will still only run when custo

entries.heading: bell-features
entries.text: Bell features to enable if bell support is available in your runtime. Not all features are available on all runtimes. The format of this is a list of features to enable separated by commas. If you prefix a feature with no- then it is disabled. If you omit a feature, its default value is used. Valid values are: system Instruct the system to notify the user using built-in system functions. This could result in an audiovisual effect, a notification, or something else entirely. audio Play a custom sound. attention (enabled by default) Request the user's attention when Gui is unfocused, until it ha

entries.heading: bell-audio-path
entries.text: If audio is an enabled bell feature, this is a path to an audio file. If the path is not absolute, it is considered relative to the directory of the configuration file that it is referenced from, or from the current working directory if this is used as a CLI flag. The path may be prefixed with ~/ to reference the user's home directory.

entries.heading: bell-audio-volume
entries.text: If audio is an enabled bell feature, this is the volume to play the audio file at (relative to the system volume). This is a floating point number ranging from 0.0 (silence) to 1.0 (as loud as possible). The default is 0.5.

entries.heading: desktop-notifications
entries.text: If true (default), applications running in the terminal can show desktop notifications using certain escape sequences such as OSC 9 or OSC 777.

entries.heading: notify-on-program-status
entries.text: Which OSC 7501 program status reports raise a desktop notification while the pane is in the background. A comma separated list of the following values, each of which can be negated by prefixing it with no-: block — the program is waiting for the user (approval, an answer, a credential). done — the program finished a piece of work. fail — the program failed and stopped. All three are enabled by default. For example, no-done keeps the blocked and failed notifications but silences finished work.

entries.heading: progress-style
entries.text: If true (default), applications running in the terminal can show graphical progress bars using the ConEmu OSC 9;4 escape sequence. If false, progress bar sequences are silently ignored.

entries.heading: bold-color
entries.text: Modifies the color used for bold text in the terminal. This can be set to a specific color, using the same format as background or foreground (e.g. #RRGGBB but other formats are also supported; see the aforementioned documentation). If a specific color is set, this color will always be used for the default bold text color. It will set the rest of the bold colors to bright. This can also be set to bright, which uses the bright color palette for bold text. For example, if the text is red, then the bold will use the bright red color. The terminal palette is set with palette but can also be overri

entries.heading: faint-opacity
entries.text: The opacity level (opposite of transparency) of the faint text. A value of 1 is fully opaque and a value of 0 is fully transparent. A value less than 0 or greater than 1 will be clamped to the nearest valid value.

entries.heading: term
entries.text: This will be used to set the TERM environment variable. HACK: We set this with an xterm prefix because vim uses that to enable key protocols (specifically this will enable modifyOtherKeys), among other features. An option exists in vim to modify this: :set keyprotocol=ghostty:kitty, however a bug in the implementation prevents it from working properly. https://github.com/vim/vim/pull/13211 fixes this.

entries.heading: enquiry-response
entries.text: String to send when we receive ENQ (0x05) from the command that we are running. Defaults to an empty string if not set.

entries.heading: clipboard-write-limit-bytes
entries.text: OSC 52 write size limit

entries.heading: drag-handle
entries.text: split drag handle visibility

entries.heading: scrollback-limit-bytes
entries.text: Gui splits Ghostty's scrollback-limit in two: this one caps bytes, scrollback-limit-lines caps rows. An integer (0x… works), unlimited, or 0 to disable scrollback.

entries.heading: scrollback-limit-lines
entries.text: Row cap for the scrollback, unlimited by default. It applies together with the byte cap; whichever is reached first trims the history.

entries.heading: link-osc8
entries.text: OSC 8 hyperlinks

entries.heading: middle-click-action
entries.text: middle click action

entries.heading: vt-window-resize-allowed
entries.text: allow window resize sequences

entries.heading: vt-xt-checksum-extension
entries.text: XT checksum extension

entries.heading: vt-xt-checksum-report
entries.text: report XT checksums

entries.heading: auto-update
entries.text: check (the default) looks for a newer release on GitHub in the background when the app launches, at most once every 24 hours, and shows a pill when one exists. off disables that launch check; "Check for Updates" in the command palette still works.

entries.heading: auto-update-channel
entries.text: stable (the default) reads the latest public release; tip also considers pre-releases.

entries.heading: 选项参考
entries.text: 该文档主要来自 Ghostty 的 Option Reference。 这里列出了 Gui 全部配置项的参考。这些选项大致按照使用频率排序， 并与相关选项分组。建议使用浏览器的搜索功能来查找你需要的选项。

entries.heading: tab-position
entries.text: 标签栏的位置 —— 顶部、左侧或右侧。

entries.heading: compact
entries.text: true（默认）时窗格紧贴排列，分隔线为 1 DIP；false 时窗格浮动显示为圆角卡片。

entries.heading: sidebar-width-left
entries.text: 左侧标签栏的宽度，单位为 DIP；拖动其边缘时，应用会把新宽度写回配置。

entries.heading: sidebar-width-right
entries.text: 右侧标签栏的宽度，单位为 DIP；拖动其边缘时，应用会把新宽度写回配置。

entries.heading: debug-tap
entries.text: 以十六进制把两个方向上原始的 VT 字节流记录到日志中。

entries.heading: crash-dumps
entries.text: 向 Windows 错误报告注册以获取完整转储，崩溃后转储文件会留在 %TEMP%\gui-dumps 中。

entries.heading: language
entries.text: Gui 图形界面的语言：en 或 zh-CN。例如： language = zh-CN 空值（默认）会跟随系统语言：简体中文系统使用中文字符串，其他语言系统使用英文。 与 Ghostty 不同，该值可以在运行时重新加载，无需重启。 这只改变 Gui 自身的界面文字，不会改变在终端内部运行的程序所使用的语言， 后者仍遵循系统默认值。

entries.heading: font-family-bold-italic
entries.text: 要使用的字体族。 你可以用 CLI 生成有效值列表： gui +list-fonts 在 Gui 自己的终端里运行该命令会打开字体浏览器：左侧列出已安装的字体族，右侧用该字体的真实字形预览；按 Enter 会把选中的字体写入配置的 font-family。输出被重定向或不在 Gui 终端里运行时，则改为每行打印一个字体族及其可用样式。 该配置可以重复多次，用于在主字体中缺少所需码位时指定首选的 回退字体。这对多语言、符号字体等场景尤其有用。 关于 emoji：Gui 用 DirectWrite 绘制文字并开启彩色字形 （EnableColorFont），所以 emoji 会以彩色字形渲染。默认的 JetBrainsMono Nerd Font 不含 emoji 字形，主字体没有覆盖的字符会交给 DirectWrite 的系统回退，在 Windows 上通常由 Segoe UI Emoji 补上。 你也可以在这里追加字体族作为回退，或用 font-codepoint-map 把指定码位固定映射到某个字体。 具体样式（粗体、斜体、粗斜体）不需要显式设置。如果某个样式没有设置， 就会在常规样式（font-family）中寻找风格变体。如果找不到风格变体， Gui 会使用常规样式。这样可以避免仅仅为了获得粗体之类的样式 而回退到其他字体族。这一点同样适用于你为某个样式显式指定字体族的情况。

entries.heading: font-style-bold-italic
entries.text: 为每个所需的终端字体样式使用的具名字体样式。它会根据字体自身 公布的字体样式字符串来查找样式。例如，"Iosevka Heavy" 的样式为 "Heavy"。 你也可以用这些字段完全禁用某个字体样式。如果你把下面配置的值设为 字面量 false，该字体样式就会被禁用。如果终端中运行的程序请求了 已被禁用的字体样式，则会改用常规字体样式。 这些配置只有在对应的 font-family 也指定时才有效。如果没有指定 font-family，那么 font-style 会被忽略，除非你是在禁用该字体样式。

entries.heading: font-synthetic-style
entries.text: 控制当指定的 font-family 中没有请求的样式时，Gui 是否应合成该样式。 如果字体没有特定样式，Gui 可以合成粗体、斜体和粗斜体样式。 对于粗体，是通过在字形周围绘制粗细可变的外轮廓来实现的。对于斜体， 是通过对字形施加倾斜来实现的。对于粗斜体，则会同时应用这两种处理。 合成样式并不完美，通常看起来不如原生具备该样式的字体。不过，当字体 没有该样式时，它们有助于提供带样式的文本。 把此项设为 "false" 或 "true" 可以完全禁用或启用合成样式。你可以使用 "no-bold"、"no-italic" 和 "no-bold-italic" 禁用特定样式。用逗号分隔 即可禁用多个样式，例如 "no-bold,no-italic"。 可用的样式键有：bold、italic、bold-italic。 如果合成样式被禁用，那么在请求的样式不可用时就会改用常规样式。如果 字体本身具有请求的样式，则会直接使用该字体，因为该样式不是合成的。 一个常见的错误是禁用了 bold 或 italic，却没有禁用 bold-italic。只禁用 bold 或 italic 并不会禁用 bold-italic 样式中的相应部分。如果你想禁用 bold-italic，必须显式禁用它。 你无法部分禁用 bold-italic。 默认情况下，合成样式处于启用状态。

entries.heading: font-feature
entries.text: 应用字体特性。要启用多个字体特性，可以重复设置多次，或使用 逗号分隔的特性设置列表。 特性设置的语法如下，其中 feat 是一个特性： 启用特性，例如 feat、+feat、feat on、feat=1。 禁用特性，例如 -feat、feat off、feat=0。 设置特性值，例如 feat=2、feat = 3、feat 4。 特性名称可以用引号包裹，这意味着此配置在语法上应兼容 font-feature-settings CSS 属性。 语法相当宽松，但无效的设置会被静默忽略。 该字体特性会应用于 Gui 渲染的所有字体。未来的增强将允许 针对特定字面（face）。 要禁用编程连字，请使用 -calt，因为这是编程连字的典型特性名。 要了解你的字体有哪些字体特性以及它们的作用，请使用字体检查工具， 例如 fontdrop.info。 要大体上禁用大多数连字，请使用 -calt, -liga, -dlig。

entries.heading: font-size
entries.text: 字体大小，以磅（point）为单位。该值可以是非整数，最终会选择最接近的 整数像素大小。如果你的高 DPI 显示器上 1pt = 2px，那么指定半个磅值 就能得到奇数像素大小。 例如，13.5pt @ 2px/pt = 27px 在运行时更改此配置只会影响那些没有以任何方式手动调整过字体大小的 现有终端（例如放大或缩小过字体）。手动调整过字体大小的终端会保留 其手动调整后的大小。除此之外，现有终端的字体大小会在重新加载时更新。

entries.heading: font-variation-bold-italic
entries.text: 一个可重复的配置，用于为可变字体设置一个或多个字体变体值。 可变字体是单个字体，其文件名通常以 -VF.ttf 或 -VF.otf 结尾， 包含一个或多个可配置轴，用于控制字重、倾斜等。并非所有字体都支持 变体；只有明确声明自己是可变字体的字体才能生效。 其格式为 id=value，其中 id 是轴标识符。轴标识符始终是 4 个字符 的字符串，例如 wght。要获取支持的轴列表，请查看字体文档或使用 字体检查工具。 无效的 id 和值通常会被忽略。例如，如果某个字体只支持 100 到 700 的字重，设置 wght=800 不会产生任何效果（不会被钳制到 700）。 你必须查阅字体文档来了解支持哪些值。 常见的轴有：wght（字重）、slnt（倾斜）、ital（斜体）、opsz （光学尺寸）、wdth（宽度）、GRAD（渐变）等。

entries.heading: font-codepoint-map
entries.text: 强制一个或一段 Unicode 码位映射到指定的具名字体。如果你想支持 特殊符号，或者想使用在你的特定字体下渲染效果更好的特定字形， 这会很有用。 语法为 codepoint=fontname，其中 codepoint 可以是单个码位或一个 范围。码位必须用完整的 Unicode 十六进制值指定，例如 U+ABCD。 码位范围的写法为 U+ABCD-U+DEFG。你可以为同一字体指定多个范围， 用逗号分隔，例如 U+ABCD-U+DEFG,U+1234-U+5678=fontname。字体名称 与你在 font-family 中使用的值相同。 此配置可以重复多次，以指定多个码位映射。 在运行时更改此配置只会影响新建的终端，即新窗口、标签页等。

entries.heading: clipboard-codepoint-map
entries.text: 在把文本复制到剪贴板时，将特定的 Unicode 码位映射为替换值。 此配置允许你在把终端内容复制到剪贴板时，用其他字符或字符串替换 特定的 Unicode 字符。这对于把特殊的终端符号转换为更兼容的字符， 以便粘贴到其他应用中很有用。 语法与 font-codepoint-map 类似： 单个码位：U+1234=U+ABCD 或 U+1234=replacement_text 码位范围：U+1234-U+5678=U+ABCD 示例： clipboard-codepoint-map = U+2500=U+002D（制表符横线 → 连字符） clipboard-codepoint-map = U+2502=U+007C（制表符竖线 → 竖线符） clipboard-codepoint-map = U+03A3=SUM（希腊字母 sigma → "SUM"） 此配置可以重复多次以指定多个映射。对于重叠的范围，后面的条目 优先于前面的条目。 这只适用于文本复制操作，不适用于 URL 复制。

entries.heading: font-shaping-break
entries.text: 把字体塑形拆分成多个 run 的位置。 "run" 是被一起塑形的一段连续文本。"塑形"（shaping）是把文本（码位） 转换为字形（可渲染字符）的过程。连字就是这样形成的。例如，如果某个 编程字体把 "!=" 变成单个字形，那么它必须在同一个 run 中看到相邻的 "!" 和 "="。当 run 被断开时，文本会被分别塑形。继续上面的例子，如果 "!" 位于一个 run 的末尾，而 "=" 位于下一个 run 的开头，那么连字就 不会形成。 Gui 会在某些位置断开 run，以提高可读性或可用性。例如，Gui 默认会在光标下方断开 run，这样文本编辑时就能看到单个字符而不是连字。 此配置让你可以控制这一行为。 用逗号组合多个值以设置多个选项。给选项加上 "no-" 前缀即可禁用它。 启用和禁用选项可以同时进行。 可用选项： cursor - 在光标下方断开 run。

entries.heading: adjust-cell-height
entries.text: 所有这些配置的行为都是调整由字体决定的各种度量值。取值可以是 整数（1、-1 等）或百分比（20%、-15% 等）。无论哪种形式，该值都 表示在原值基础上改变的量。 例如，取值 1 会把该值增加 1，而不是把它字面设置为 1。取值 20% 会把该值增加 20%，依此类推。 这些值几乎没有校验，因此错误的值（例如 -100%）可能让终端无法使用。 请谨慎且合理地使用。 部分取值会被钳制到最小值或最大值。这会让某些值看起来被忽略了。 例如，许多 -thickness 调整不能低于 1px。 adjust-cell-height 还有一些额外的行为需要说明： 字体将在单元格中垂直居中。 光标会保持与字体相同的大小，但可以通过 adjust-cursor-height 单独调整。 Powerline 字形会随单元格高度一起调整，从而让状态栏之类的 内容继续保持对齐。

entries.heading: adjust-font-baseline
entries.text: 从单元格底部到文本基线的距离调整，单位为像素或百分比。 增大该值会把基线向上移动，减小则向下移动。 关于调整的说明请参阅 adjust-cell-width。

entries.heading: adjust-underline-position
entries.text: 从单元格顶部到下划线上边缘的距离调整，单位为像素或百分比。 增大该值会把下划线向下移动，减小则向上移动。 关于调整的说明请参阅 adjust-cell-width。

entries.heading: adjust-underline-thickness
entries.text: 下划线的粗细，单位为像素。 关于调整的说明请参阅 adjust-cell-width。

entries.heading: adjust-strikethrough-position
entries.text: 从单元格顶部到删除线上边缘的距离调整，单位为像素或百分比。 增大该值会把删除线向下移动，减小则向上移动。 关于调整的说明请参阅 adjust-cell-width。

entries.heading: adjust-strikethrough-thickness
entries.text: 删除线的粗细调整，单位为像素或百分比。 关于调整的说明请参阅 adjust-cell-width。

entries.heading: adjust-overline-position
entries.text: 从单元格顶部到上划线上边缘的距离调整，单位为像素或百分比。 增大该值会把上划线向下移动，减小则向上移动。 关于调整的说明请参阅 adjust-cell-width。

entries.heading: adjust-overline-thickness
entries.text: 上划线的粗细调整，单位为像素或百分比。 关于调整的说明请参阅 adjust-cell-width。

entries.heading: adjust-cursor-thickness
entries.text: 条形光标和描边矩形光标的粗细调整，单位为像素或百分比。 关于调整的说明请参阅 adjust-cell-width。

entries.heading: adjust-cursor-height
entries.text: 光标的高度调整，单位为像素或百分比。目前适用于所有光标类型： bar、rect 和 outlined rect。 关于调整的说明请参阅 adjust-cell-width。

entries.heading: adjust-box-thickness
entries.text: 制表符字符的粗细调整，单位为像素或百分比。 关于调整的说明请参阅 adjust-cell-width。

entries.heading: adjust-icon-height
entries.text: nerd font 图标最大高度的调整，单位为像素或百分比。 正值（负值）会增大（减小）图标的最大高度。这未必会同等影响所有 图标：效果取决于图标的默认大小是否受高度约束，而这又取决于图标 和主字体两者的宽高比。 某些为制表符绘制和终端图形设计的图标（例如 Powerline 符号） 不受此选项影响。 关于调整的说明请参阅 adjust-cell-width。

entries.heading: theme
entries.text: 要使用的主题：内置主题名称，或 themes 文件夹中的文件名。Gui 还支持 分别为浅色和深色模式指定不同的主题。 主题名按文件名解析：先找配置文件旁的 themes 文件夹 （%APPDATA%\gui\themes），再找可执行文件旁内置的 Assets\Themes\light 和 Assets\Themes\dark。自己文件夹里的同名主题会 覆盖内置主题。名称不能包含路径分隔符，theme 只接受名字而不是路径。 要查看可用主题列表，请运行 gui +list-themes。 主题文件只设置颜色：background、foreground、cursor-color、 selection-background、selection-foreground 和 palette。文件必须同时 设置 background 和 foreground 才会被加载，其它键会被忽略，因此主题 不能改变行为，也不能引入其他文件。请不要使用来自不受信任来源的主题文件。 通过 background、foreground、palette 等指定的任何额外颜色都会覆盖 主题中指定的颜色。 要为浅色和深色模式指定不同的主题，请使用以下语法： light:theme-name,dark:theme-name。例如： light:Rose Pine Dawn,dark:Rose Pine。所有值周围的空白

entries.heading: background
entries.text: 窗口的背景色。 可用十六进制（#RRGGBB 或 RRGGBB）或具名的 X11 颜色指定。

entries.heading: foreground
entries.text: 窗口的前景色。 可用十六进制（#RRGGBB 或 RRGGBB）或具名的 X11 颜色指定。

entries.heading: background-image
entries.text: 终端的背景图像。 这应当是一个 PNG 或 JPEG 文件的路径，其他图像格式尚不支持。 背景图像目前是按终端而不是按窗口生效的。 解码后的位图由同一进程内的所有分屏共享，不会在显存中重复一份。

entries.heading: background-image-opacity
entries.text: 背景图像的不透明度。 这是相对于 background-opacity 的值而言的。 Gui 的处理与 Ghostty 不同：取值限定在 0.0 到 1.0，大于 1.0 会按 1.0 处理。图片会以“本值 × background-opacity”的不透明度，叠加在面板 背景之上。 默认 background-opacity = 1.0 时，图片就是直接盖在背景色上。背景不透明 度较低时，图片叠在已经半透明的面板之上，因此看起来会比面板背景明显更不 透明。 Ghostty 则是先把图片与背景色合成，再整体应用 background-opacity，并且 允许大于 1.0 的取值。

entries.heading: background-image-position
entries.text: 背景图像的位置。 有效值： top-left top-center top-right center-left center center-right bottom-left bottom-center bottom-right 默认值为 center。

entries.heading: background-image-fit
entries.text: 背景图像的适配方式。 有效值： contain 保持宽高比，把背景图像缩放到仍能完整容纳在终端内的最大尺寸， 使整幅图像都可见。 cover 保持宽高比，把背景图像缩放到能完全覆盖终端的最小尺寸。这可能导致 图像的一条或多条边缘被终端边缘裁掉。 stretch 把背景图像拉伸到终端的完整大小，不保持宽高比。 none 不缩放背景图像。 默认值为 contain。

entries.heading: background-image-repeat
entries.text: 是否重复背景图像。 如果设为 true，当背景图像未完全填满终端区域而在其周围留有空白的 情况下，就会重复该背景图像。 默认值为 false。

entries.heading: selection-background
entries.text: 选区的前景色和背景色。如果没有设置，选区颜色就是反转后的窗口背景色 和前景色（注意：不要与单元格的前景/背景色混淆）。 可用十六进制（#RRGGBB 或 RRGGBB）或具名的 X11 颜色指定。

entries.heading: selection-clear-on-typing
entries.text: 输入时是否清除选中的文本。默认值为 true。这也是大多数终端模拟器 以及文本输入框的典型行为。如果把它设为 false，输入时选中的文本 不会被清除。 “输入”特指任何能产生数据并发送给终端内运行的应用（例如 shell）的 非修饰键（shift、control、alt 等）按键。此外，当任何预编辑或组合 输入状态开始时（例如输入日语等语言时），选区也会被清除。 如果此项为 false，仍可以通过单击一次或按 escape 手动清除选区。

entries.heading: selection-clear-on-copy
entries.text: 复制后是否清除选中的文本。默认值为 false。 设为 true 时，在调用 copy_to_clipboard 键盘绑定的任何复制操作 之后，选区都会被自动清除。需要注意的是，如果复制操作是通过 copy-on-select 触发的，则不会清除选区。 设为 false 时，复制后选区仍然可见，可以看清复制了什么，也可能 对同一选区执行其他操作。

entries.heading: selection-word-chars
entries.text: 在文本选择操作（例如双击）中标记单词边界的字符。选择单词时， 选区会在这些字符中的任意一个处停止。 这类似于 zsh 中的 WORDCHARS 环境变量，区别在于这里指定的是边界 字符而不是单词字符。默认值包含在代码和普通文本中通常用于分隔单词 的常见分隔符和标点。 此字符串中的每个字符都会成为一个单词边界。支持多字节 UTF-8 字符， 但只能指定单个码位。不支持多码位序列（例如 emoji）。 空字符（U+0000）始终被视为边界，无需包含在此配置中。 默认值：` \t'"│ :;,()[]{}<>$ ` 要添加或移除特定字符，可以把它设为一个自定义值。例如，要把分号 视为单词的一部分： selection-word-chars = " \t'\"│ :,()[]{}<>$"

entries.heading: minimum-contrast
entries.text: 前景色和背景色之间的最小对比度。对比度是介于 1 和 21 之间的值。 值为 1 表示允许没有对比度（例如黑底黑字）。该值是 WCAG 2.0 规范中定义的对比度。 如果你想避免出现不可见的文本（颜色与背景相同），1.1 是一个不错的 取值。如果你想避免出现难以阅读的文本，3 或更高的值是不错的选择。 值越高，文本越有可能变成黑色或白色。 此值不适用于 Emoji 或图像。

entries.heading: palette
entries.text: 许多终端应用使用的 256 色形式的调色板。此配置的语法为 N=COLOR， 其中 N 是 0 到 255（对应终端颜色表中的 256 种颜色），COLOR 是 常见的 RGB 颜色代码，例如 #AABBCC 或 AABBCC，也可以是具名的 X11 颜色。例如，palette = 5=#BB78D9 会设置“紫色”。 调色板索引可以使用十进制、二进制、八进制或十六进制。除非使用前缀， 否则默认按十进制处理：0b 表示二进制，0o 表示八进制，0x 表示 十六进制。 关于颜色索引的定义以及它们规范上对应的颜色， 请参阅此速查表。 对于大多数主题，你只需要设置前 16 种颜色（0–15），因为调色板的 其余部分（16–255）默认会自动生成（详情请参阅 palette-generate）。

entries.heading: palette-generate
entries.text: 是否从 16 种基础 ANSI 颜色自动生成扩展的 256 色调色板 （索引 16–255）。 这让主题作者只需指定 16 种基础颜色，其余调色板部分就会以一致且 美观的方式自动生成。 启用后，6×6×6 色立方和 24 级灰度渐变会从基础调色板的插值中得出， 从而获得更协调的外观。通过 palette 显式设置的颜色永远不会被覆盖。 默认值为 false（禁用），因为许多使用 256 色调色板的传统程序都硬编码 了关于这些颜色是什么的假设（大多假定为 xterm 256 色调色板）。不过， 对于想要自定义调色板又不想指定全部 256 种颜色的主题作者和用户来说， 这仍然是一个非常有用的工具。 关于生成方式的更多信息，请参见： https://gist.github.com/jake-stewart/0a8ea46159a7da2c808e5be2177e1783

entries.heading: palette-harmonious
entries.text: 反转启用 palette-generate 时生成的调色板颜色，使颜色按相反顺序 排列。这使基于调色板的应用在浅色和深色模式下都能良好工作，因为 这些调色板始终是相对较好的颜色。 此项默认关闭，因为某些传统终端应用硬编码了调色板索引 16–231 按从暗到亮排序的假设，启用此项会让它们无法阅读。这并不是一个 普遍合理的假设，我们鼓励现代终端应用以更具语义的方式使用索引。 如果 palette-generate 被禁用，此项没有任何效果。 更多信息请参阅 palette-generate。

entries.heading: cursor-color
entries.text: 光标的颜色。如果没有设置，会选择一个默认值。 可以直接用十六进制（#RRGGBB 或 RRGGBB）或具名的 X11 颜色指定 颜色。 此外，还可以使用特殊值让颜色在运行时与其他颜色匹配： cell-foreground - 匹配单元格前景色。 cell-background - 匹配单元格背景色。

entries.heading: cursor-opacity
entries.text: 光标的不透明度（透明度的反面）。值为 1 表示完全不透明，值为 0 表示完全透明。小于 0 或大于 1 的值会被钳制到最接近的有效值。 注意，像 0.3 这样足够小的值可能实际上几乎不可见，并可能让你很难 找到光标。

entries.heading: cursor-style
entries.text: 光标的样式。这会设置默认样式。运行中的程序仍可以通过转义序列 （例如 CSI q）请求显式的光标样式。shell 配置通常会请求特定的 光标样式。 注意，无论此配置如何，shell 集成都会在提示符处自动把光标设为条形。 你可以通过指定 shell-integration-features = no-cursor 或完全禁用 shell 集成来禁用该行为。 有效值： block bar underline block_hollow

entries.heading: cursor-style-blink
entries.text: 设置光标的默认闪烁状态。这只是默认状态；运行中的程序可以使用 DECSCUSR（CSI q）覆盖光标样式。 如果没有设置此项，光标默认不闪烁。把它设为 true 才会闪烁。 有效值是： （空白） true false

entries.heading: cursor-text
entries.text: 光标下方文本的颜色。如果没有设置，会选择一个默认值。 可用十六进制（#RRGGBB 或 RRGGBB）或具名的 X11 颜色指定。 还可以设为 cell-foreground 以匹配单元格前景色， 或设为 cell-background 以匹配单元格背景色。

entries.heading: mouse-hide-while-typing
entries.text: 输入时立即隐藏鼠标。使用鼠标（按键、移动等）时，鼠标会重新可见。

entries.heading: scroll-to-bottom
entries.text: 何时把表面滚动到底部。其格式是用逗号分隔的待启用选项列表。如果给 某个选项加上 no- 前缀，则禁用该选项。如果省略某个选项，则使用其 默认值。 可用选项： keystroke 如果设置，当用户按下会导致数据发送到 PTY 的按键时 （基本上除修饰键或由 Gui 处理的键绑定之外的任何按键），把 表面滚动到底部。 output 如果设置，当有新数据需要显示时（例如向终端打印新行时）， 把表面滚动到底部。 默认值为 keystroke, no-output。

entries.heading: mouse-shift-capture
entries.text: 决定运行中的程序能否检测到与鼠标点击同时按下的 shift 键。通常， shift 键用于扩展鼠标选区。 默认值 false 意味着 shift 键不会随鼠标协议发送，并会扩展选区。 运行中的程序可以通过 XTSHIFTESCAPE 序列有条件地覆盖此值。 值 true 意味着 shift 键会随鼠标协议发送，但运行中的程序可以通过 XTSHIFTESCAPE 覆盖此行为。 值 never 与 false 相同，但运行中的程序无法通过 XTSHIFTESCAPE 覆盖此行为。值 always 与 true 相同，但运行中的程序无法通过 XTSHIFTESCAPE 覆盖此行为。 如果你希望即使程序另有请求，shift 也始终扩展鼠标选区，请把此项 设为 never。 有效值： true false always never

entries.heading: mouse-reporting
entries.text: 启用或禁用鼠标报告。设为 false 时，即使终端应用请求，鼠标事件也 不会被报告给它们。这让你始终能把鼠标用于选区和其他终端 UI 交互， 而不会被应用捕获鼠标输入。 设为 true（默认）时，终端应用可以请求鼠标报告，并会按照其请求的 模式接收鼠标事件。 这可以在运行时使用 toggle_mouse_reporting 键绑定动作切换。

entries.heading: mouse-scroll-multiplier
entries.text: 鼠标滚轮滚动距离的乘数。 可以使用 precision: 或 discrete: 前缀，只为特定类型的设备设置 乘数。可以用逗号分隔以同时设置两种类型的乘数，例如 precision:0.1,discrete:3。如果未使用前缀，乘数适用于所有滚动设备。 指定前缀的功能在 Ghostty 1.2.1 中引入。 该值会被钳制到 [0.01, 10,000]。这两个都是极端值，如果你设置任一 极端值，很可能会有糟糕的体验。 对于离散设备，默认值为 "3"；对于精确设备，默认值为 "1"。 Gui 每个滚轮刻度滚动的行数（默认 3）。precision 形式可以被接受，但 Windows 的滚轮属于离散设备。

entries.heading: background-opacity
entries.text: 背景的不透明度（透明度的反面）。值为 1 表示完全不透明，值为 0 表示完全透明。小于 0 或大于 1 的值会被钳制到最接近的有效值。 Gui 低于 1 时，整个窗口（包括窗口边框）会被统一着色一次，而不是叠加在系统亚克力效果之上；background-blur 决定使用亚克力还是纯色着色。

entries.heading: background-opacity-cells
entries.text: 对显式设置了背景色的单元格应用背景不透明度。 通常，background-opacity 只应用于窗口背景。如果某个单元格显式设置 了背景色（例如红色），那么该背景色将是完全不透明的。由此产生的一个 结果是，某些会重绘终端背景色的终端应用（例如 Neovim 和 Tmux） 可能不会遵循 background-opacity（这是有意设计的）。 把此项设为 true 会对所有单元格应用 background-opacity，无论它们 是否显式设置了背景色。

entries.heading: background-blur
entries.text: 当 background-opacity 小于 1 时是否模糊背景。 有效值： 一个非负整数，指定模糊强度 false，等同于模糊强度 0 true，等同于默认模糊强度 20，对于好看的模糊效果而言这是 合理的取值。更高的模糊强度可能导致渲染异常和性能问题。 Gui true 使用亚克力；在 Windows 11 上 false 会绘制未经模糊的着色（Windows 10 仍保留亚克力，与 Windows Terminal 的行为一致）。

entries.heading: unfocused-split-opacity
entries.text: 未聚焦分屏的不透明度（透明度的反面）。未聚焦的分屏默认会略微淡化， 以便更容易看出哪个分屏处于聚焦状态。要禁用此功能，请把此值设为 1。 值为 1 表示完全不透明，值为 0 表示完全透明。由于“0”没有用处 （会让窗口看起来非常怪异），最小值是 0.15。这个值看起来仍然很怪异， 但至少能看清发生了什么。超出 0.15 到 1 范围的值会被钳制到最接近的 有效值。

entries.heading: unfocused-split-fill
entries.text: 用于让未聚焦分屏变暗的颜色。未聚焦分屏是通过在该分屏上渲染一个 半透明矩形来变暗的。此项设置该矩形的颜色，可用于精细控制变暗效果。 默认值为背景色。 可用十六进制（#RRGGBB 或 RRGGBB）或具名的 X11 颜色指定。

entries.heading: split-divider-color
entries.text: 分屏分隔线的颜色。如果没有设置，会选择一个默认值。 可用十六进制（#RRGGBB 或 RRGGBB）或具名的 X11 颜色指定。

entries.heading: search-background
entries.text: 搜索匹配项的前景色和背景色。这只适用于未聚焦的搜索匹配项，也称为 候选匹配项。 有效值： 十六进制（#RRGGBB 或 RRGGBB） 具名的 X11 颜色 "cell-foreground"，以匹配单元格前景色 "cell-background"，以匹配单元格背景色 默认值为金黄色背景上的黑色文本。

entries.heading: search-selected-background
entries.text: 当前选中的搜索匹配项的前景色和背景色。这是使用下一个/上一个搜索 导航时会跳转到的聚焦匹配项。 有效值： 十六进制（#RRGGBB 或 RRGGBB） 具名的 X11 颜色 "cell-foreground"，以匹配单元格前景色 "cell-background"，以匹配单元格背景色 默认值为柔和桃色背景上的黑色文本。

entries.heading: command
entries.text: 要运行的命令，通常是一个 shell。如果它不是绝对路径，会在 PATH 中 查找。如果没有设置，会从你的系统中查找一个默认值。默认查找规则是： SHELL 环境变量 passwd 条目（用户信息） 其中可以包含运行该命令的附加参数。如果提供了附加参数，命令会使用 /bin/sh -c 执行，以便交给 shell 进行参数展开。 要完全避免 shell 展开，请在命令前加上 direct:，例如 direct:nvim foo。这会避免往返调用 /bin/sh，但也不支持任何 shell 解析，例如带空格的参数、包含 ~ 的文件路径、通配符等。 你也可以显式地在命令前加上 shell:，以始终把命令包裹在 shell 中。 这可用于确保在我们选择正确模式的启发式判断有误时不会使用它们。 该命令会用于所有新建的终端表面，即新窗口、标签页等。如果你只想为 Gui 启动时创建的第一个终端表面运行命令，请使用 initial-command 配置。 Gui 支持常见的 -e 标志，用于执行带参数的命令。例如 gui -e fish --with --custom --args。该标志会设置 initial-command 配置，更多信息请参阅该项。

entries.heading: initial-command
entries.text: 这与 "command" 相同，但只适用于 Gui 启动时创建的第一个终端表面。 后续的终端表面会使用 command 配置。 在第一个终端表面创建（或关闭）之后，就无法再自动运行此初始命令。 因此，在运行时设置此项虽然有效，但只有在它是有史以来创建的 第一个终端表面时才会对其生效。 如果从命令行启动 Gui，-e 是设置此项的快捷方式：它后面的所有参数 都会作为命令。例如：gui -e fish --with --custom --args。

entries.heading: notify-on-command-finish
entries.text: 控制何时发送命令完成通知。共有三个选项： never - 从不发送通知。 unfocused - 仅在命令运行的表面未聚焦时发送通知（默认）。 always - 始终发送通知。 命令完成通知需要启用 shell 集成，或者你的 shell 会发送 OSC 133 转义序列来标记命令的开始和结束。

entries.heading: notify-on-command-finish-action
entries.text: 如果启用了命令完成通知，此项控制如何通知用户。 可用选项： bell - 默认启用 notify - 默认启用 选项可以通过以逗号分隔的列表组合使用。选项可以加上 no- 前缀来 取反。例如 no-bell,notify。

entries.heading: notify-on-command-finish-after
entries.text: 如果启用了命令完成通知，此项控制命令必须运行多久才会发送通知。 默认值为五秒。 时长由一系列数字后跟时间单位组成。数字和单位之间允许有空白。 每个数字和单位会相加构成总时长。 允许的时间单位如下： y - 365 个 SI 天，即 8760 小时，或 31536000 秒。不会针对 闰年或闰秒做调整。 d - 一个 SI 天，即 86400 秒。 h - 一小时，即 3600 秒。 m - 一分钟，即 60 秒。 s - 一秒。 ms - 一毫秒，即 0.001 秒。 us 或 µs - 一微秒，即 0.000001 秒。 ns - 一纳秒，即 0.000000001 秒。 示例： 1h30m 45s 单位可以重复，并会相加。这意味着 1h1h 等同于 2h。这会令人 困惑，应当避免。未来的更新可能会禁止这种写法。 最大值为 584y 49w 23h 34m 33s 709ms 551µs 615ns。任何大于该值的 值都会被钳制到最大值。

entries.heading: env
entries.text: 传给在终端表面中启动的命令的额外环境变量。格式为 env=KEY=VALUE。 env = foo=bar env = bar=baz 把 env 设为空字符串会把整个映射重置为默认值（空）。 env = 把一个键设为空字符串会从映射中移除该键及其对应的值。 env = foo=bar env = foo= 会导致 foo 不会被传给所启动的命令。 多次设置同一个键会覆盖之前的条目。 env = foo=bar env = foo=baz 会导致 foo=baz 被传给所启动的命令。 这些环境变量会覆盖 Gui 设置的任何现有环境变量。例如，在这里设置 TERM_PROGRAM 会覆盖 Gui 通常自动注入的 Gui 值。 这些环境变量_不会_被传给 Gui 为其他目的运行命令时所用的命令， 例如用于在浏览器中打开 URL 的 open 或 xdg-open。

entries.heading: input
entries.text: 启动时作为输入发送给命令的数据。 配置的 command 会按通常规则启动，然后在可以提供任何其他输入之前， 此处指定的数据会被写入 pty。 字节会按原样发送，不附加任何编码。因此，对可能包含控制字符的输入 要格外小心，因为这可能被用来在 shell 中执行程序。 此值的格式为： raw: - 按原样发送原始文本。它使用 Zig 字符串字面量 语法，因此可以指定控制字符和其他标准转义。 path: - 读取文件路径并发送其内容。路径必须指向长度有限 的文件，例如不要使用 /dev/stdin 或 /dev/urandom 之类的设备， 因为它们会无限期阻塞终端启动。为防止过度占用内存，文件大小 限制为 10MB。如果你有更大的文件，应编写脚本来读取该文件并 发送到终端。 如果没有找到有效前缀，则假定为 raw: 输入。这是一个易用性设计， 让你可以简单地写 input = "Hello, world!"（常见情况），而无需给 每个值都加上 raw: 前缀。 此配置可以重复多次以发送更多数据。数据会直接拼接，中间没有分隔 字符（例如没有换行符）。 如果任何一个输入来源不存在，则不会发送任何输入。输入来源直到终端 启动时才会验证，因此缺失的路径不会在配置验证中显示出来。 在运行时更改此配置只会影响新建的终端。

entries.heading: wait-after-command
entries.text: 如果为 true，命令退出后保持终端打开。通常，运行中的命令（例如 shell） 退出时终端窗口会关闭。如果此项为 true，终端窗口会保持打开，直到 收到任意按键。 这主要用于脚本或调试。

entries.heading: abnormal-command-exit-runtime
entries.text: 运行时长低于多少毫秒时，我们认为进程退出属于异常。这用于在进程 过快退出时显示错误消息。

entries.heading: scrollbar
entries.text: 控制何时显示用于滚动回滚缓冲区的滚动条。 默认值为 system。 有效值： system - 遵循关于何时显示滚动条的系统设置。 never - 从不显示滚动条。你仍然可以使用鼠标、键绑定动作等 进行滚动，但不会有显示滚动条的可见 UI 控件。

entries.heading: link-url
entries.text: 启用 URL 匹配。URL 会在按住 Ctrl 悬停时匹配，并使用链接 URL 对应的 默认系统应用打开。 Gui 只匹配 URL，没有自定义链接规则。

entries.heading: link-previews
entries.text: 显示匹配 URL 的链接预览。 为 true 时，会为所有匹配的 URL 显示链接预览。为 false 时，从不显示 链接预览。设为 "osc8" 时，只会为使用 OSC 8 序列创建的超链接显示 链接预览（在这种情况下，链接文本可以与链接目标不同）。

entries.heading: maximize
entries.text: 是否以最大化状态启动窗口。此设置适用于新窗口，不适用于标签页、 分屏等。不过，此设置会适用于所有新窗口，而不仅是第一个窗口。

entries.heading: fullscreen
entries.text: 以全屏状态启动新窗口。此设置适用于新窗口，不适用于标签页、分屏等。 不过，此设置会适用于所有新窗口，而不仅是第一个窗口。 允许的值： false - 不以全屏启动（默认） true - 以原生全屏启动

entries.heading: title
entries.text: Gui 为窗口使用的标题。这会强制窗口标题始终为此标题，并且 Gui 会忽略程序（例如 Neovim）可能发送的任何设置标题的转义序列。 如果你想要空白标题，请用引号把这个值设为空格。例如 title = " "。 这实际上会隐藏标题。之所以需要这样做，是因为把值设为空白会把标题 重置为运行中程序的默认值。 此配置可以在运行时重新加载。如果设置了它，所有窗口的标题都会更新。 如果取消设置，下一个标题变更转义序列会被遵循，但之前的更改不会 追溯性地设置。后一种情况可能需要你重启 Neovim 之类的程序才能获得 新标题。

entries.heading: working-directory
entries.text: 启动命令后要切换到的目录。 此设置次于 window-inherit-working-directory 设置。如果同一进程中 存在先前的 Gui 终端，window-inherit-working-directory 会优先。 否则会使用此设置。通常，此设置只用于第一个窗口。 默认值为 inherit。 此值必须是绝对路径、以 ~/ 为前缀的路径（波浪号会展开为用户的主 目录），或以下特殊值之一： home - 执行用户的主目录。 inherit - 启动进程的工作目录。

entries.heading: keybind
entries.text: 键绑定。格式为 trigger=action。重复的触发器会覆盖之前设置的值。 动作列表见动作参考。 触发器：用 + 分隔的按键和修饰键列表。例如：ctrl+a、 ctrl+shift+b、up。 如果按键是单个 Unicode 码位，触发器会匹配任何产生该码位的按键。 这些会受到键盘布局的影响。例如，a 会匹配 QWERTY 键盘上的 a 键，但在 AZERTY 键盘上会匹配 q 键（假设为美式物理布局）。 对于 Unicode 码位，匹配是通过把修饰键集合与未修改的码位进行比较来 完成的。未修改的码位在其他软件中有时称为“未加 shift 的字符”，但这里 会考虑所有修饰键，而不仅是 shift。例如，ctrl+a 会匹配 a，但不会 匹配 ctrl+shift+a（在美式键盘上即 A）。 此外，码位匹配不区分大小写，未修改的码位在比较前始终会进行大小写 折叠。因此，配置了 ctrl+A 时，按下 ctrl+a 也会匹配。注意，这意味 着某些按键组合会因键盘布局而变得不可能。例如，ctrl+_ 在美式键盘上 是不可能的，因为 _ 是 shift+-，而 ctrl+shift+- 不等于 ctrl+_ （因为修饰键不匹配！）。关于不可能的按键组合的更多细节，可参阅 Qt 开发者撰写的这份极好的资料： https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qkeysequence.html

entries.heading: key-remap
